response.sql: WITH t AS (SELECT p.throws, COUNT(*) AS n FROM manager_award m JOIN player p ON p.player_id = m.player_id GROUP BY p.throws), s AS (SELECT throws, n, n * 1.0 / SUM(n) OVER () AS share FROM t), a AS (SELECT throws, n, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(n) AS combined_tally, AVG(share) AS average_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_average_share FROM a WHERE share > avg_share

assumptions.assumption: The 'average share' benchmark is the mean of the per-hand shares across all throwing-hand groups, including the NULL group (so 1 divided by the number of groups). It is not a pooled or weighted figure.

Each row in manager_award counts as one award winner, so a player who won several times is counted several times. Inner join to player on player_id drops unmatched rows, and player_id is assumed unique in player.
'Their average share' is the mean share of only the above-average hands, and 'how far above' is the mean of (share - average share) over those same hands.
